claim: Commodity GPUs communicate only over PCIe 3.0 at 16 GB/s versus up to 900 GB/s on NVLink, and they lack GPUDirect P2P, so every inter-GPU byte is routed GPU to CPU DRAM to GPU and concurrent transfers contend at the CPU root complex.
stance_target: the repo's premise that the fabric is the binding constraint and that all traffic is host-staged
scope_conditions: commodity GPU servers (3090-Ti class), PCIe 3.0 x8, no GPUDirect P2P
quoted_support: Unlike data center GPUs equipped with NVLink, which delivers a bandwidth of up to 900 GB/s, commodity GPUs can only communicate with other GPUs using PCIe-3.0 with a bandwidth of 16 GB/s... Since commodity GPUs lack GPUDirect peer to peer (GPUDirect P2P) support, inter-GPU communication is first routed through CPU to DRAM and then transferred to the target GPU.

claim: DeepSpeed ZeRO on commodity GPUs generates communication traffic of 7.3x the model size in a single training step, and communication accounts for over 70% of total training time.
stance_target: the repo's claim that FSDP/ZeRO-class data parallelism is communication-bound on this fabric and costs multiples of the model size per step
scope_conditions: 4x 3090-Ti server, GPT-like 15B model, ZeRO-3 with heterogeneous memory
quoted_support: Experimentally, we profile DeepSpeed with a GPT-like model on a 4x3090-Ti server and find that communication time accounts for over 70% of total training time... Through profiling, we find that the communication traffic of DeepSpeed is horribly 7.3x of the model size in a single training step.

claim: On commodity GPU servers most DeepSpeed data transfers reach only 50% of the CPU root complex's maximum bandwidth, because massive all-to-all collectives make multiple GPUs under the same root complex transfer simultaneously.
stance_target: the claim that contention, not just nominal link width, halves achievable collective bandwidth on a PCIe box
scope_conditions: 4x 3090-Ti, every two GPUs share a CPU root complex, 15B model fine-tune
quoted_support: We observe that most data communication of DeepSpeed only reaches 50% of the maximum bandwidth of the CPU root complex. The reason is that all GPU communications must go through the CPU's root complex due to the lack of GPUDirect P2P.

claim: Pipeline parallelism with heterogeneous memory reduces training time by 3.8-5.1x versus GPipe and DeepSpeed on commodity GPU servers across 3B to 51B models.
stance_target: the claim that PP is the correct topology for a no-P2P PCIe box, not DDP
scope_conditions: 8x 3090-Ti (24 GB), PCIe 3.0 x8, four GPUs per root complex, three topologies (Topo 4 / 2+2 / 1+3), sequence length 512, models 3B/8B/15B/51B
quoted_support: Experiments on various scale models and GPU topologies show that Mobius significantly reduces the training time by 3.8-5.1x compared with the prior art.

claim: Mobius's cross-mapping scheme deliberately places adjacent pipeline stages on GPUs under DIFFERENT CPU root complexes, because GPUs sharing a root complex contend for the same bandwidth when prefetching stages simultaneously.
stance_target: the claim that PCIe topology (which slot hangs off which root complex) determines achievable PP throughput, so the box's slot layout is a first-class experimental variable
scope_conditions: multi-root-complex commodity servers; pipeline stage-to-GPU mapping
quoted_support: Our key idea is to prevent GPUs under the same root complex from transferring data simultaneously, where possible. With this key idea, Mobius tries the best to map two adjacent stages to two GPUs under different CPU root complexes; we call this cross mapping scheme.

claim: Pipeline parallelism transfers only small activations and activation gradients between adjacent GPUs, which is why it brings remarkably fewer communications than ZeRO data parallelism on a bandwidth-starved fabric.
stance_target: the repo's claim that PP is viable where DDP/FSDP is not, because PP's per-step traffic is O(activations) rather than O(parameters)
scope_conditions: pipeline-parallel training with stages on separate GPUs
quoted_support: Mobius leverages a key observation: traditional pipeline parallelism is more suited for commodity GPUs than the existing system's ZeRO data parallelism, since it only transfers small activations and activation gradients between adjacent GPUs, bringing remarkably fewer communications.

claim: A 3B model with batch size 2 is the largest model that GPipe and DeepSpeed with pipeline parallelism can train on a 24 GB commodity GPU, and a transformer block with a 9216 hidden dimension is the largest block a single such GPU can hold during training.
stance_target: the per-card model-size ceiling for GPU-resident training, as a reference point for what must be offloaded on 64 GB cards
quoted_support: The 3B model with batch size of 2 is the largest model that GPipe and DeepSpeed with pipeline parallelism can train. The Transformer block with a 9216 hidden dimension is the largest block a single GPU can hold during training.
